title: Major offline upgrade to Fred for better deck and Clash Royale Q&A coverage

requirements.text: Expand Fred’s offline Clash Royale knowledge base significantly beyond the current topics so he can answer a much broader range of Clash Royale questions (while remaining fully deterministic and fully local with zero network calls). Add substantial new topic coverage (with keywords + synonyms + answers) for common cards, archetypes, matchups, ladder fundamentals, progression terms, and practical decision-making scenarios, so users experience a clear capability jump compared to the current limited deck answers.

quotes: I want an all new update for Fred i want like a Fred 100 I want him to have the same abilities as ChatGPT and be able to answer any clash question because right now he can barely answer simple questions about a deck I want him upgraded like 1 million lines of code

acceptanceCriteria: Fred continues to generate answers locally using the existing deterministic knowledge-base approach (no external APIs, no LLM calls).

The topic dataset (e.g., in the existing static topics module) is expanded with a clearly larger set of topic entries than the current baseline, including at minimum: (a) more deck-building guidance (roles, spell packages, defensive cores), (b) matchup/general counterplay advice for common win conditions, and (c) card-specific guidance for a meaningful set of commonly referenced cards.

Asking varied Clash Royale questions (mechanics, archetypes, counters, deck-building, general strategy) yields relevant answers more often than the current baseline, with fewer fallbacks for common questions.
All new user-facing topic content is in English.

requirements.text: Improve Fred’s ability to answer deck-related questions by adding deterministic deck-question handling that can recognize when a user provides a deck list (8 cards or near-8 cards) or asks for deck feedback, and return a structured response (identified win condition(s), likely archetype, strengths, weaknesses, and concrete improvement suggestions) based on a local, static set of rules and card-role mappings.

quotes: because right now he can barely answer simple questions about a deck

acceptanceCriteria: When the user message contains a recognizable deck list (e.g., multiple card names separated by commas/new lines), Fred produces a deck review response rather than falling back to generic topic text.

Deck review responses are deterministic and include at least: detected win condition(s), inferred archetype (or best guess), at least 2 strengths, at least 2 weaknesses, and at least 2 actionable suggestions (e.g., add a small spell, add a building, improve air defense) based only on local rules.
If the deck list is incomplete/ambiguous, Fred asks a clarifying question (e.g., “Can you list all 8 cards?”) instead of returning an unrelated answer.
No network calls are introduced; all logic runs client-side.

requirements.text: Enhance Fred’s deterministic matching so common deck/card phrasing is routed to the right answers more reliably, including handling card-name variations, punctuation, pluralization, and common shorthand (e.g., “xbow” vs “x-bow”, “gy” vs “graveyard”), while preserving deterministic behavior.

quotes: be able to answer any clash question

acceptanceCriteria: Common shorthand and minor misspellings/formatting differences for popular archetypes and win conditions (e.g., xbow/X-Bow, gy/Graveyard, bridgespam/bridge spam) match the intended topics more consistently than before.
Deck/card-oriented questions are less likely to hit the generic fallback when the relevant content exists in the knowledge base.
All matching remains deterministic (no randomness, no nondeterministic ranking).

requirements.text: Update the Ask Fred UI helper text (welcome intro and in-chat helper text) and the Fred disclaimer copy (where currently shown) so the app clearly communicates the upgraded coverage while still being accurate: Fred remains an offline, deterministic helper (not ChatGPT), may not know everything, and will ask clarifying questions when needed.

quotes: I want him to have the same abilities as ChatGPT

acceptanceCriteria: The Ask Fred welcome/intro screen text and the in-chat helper text are updated to reflect expanded coverage (including improved deck help) without claiming ChatGPT-like/open-ended internet knowledge.
The disclaimer messaging remains consistent with the existing safety stance (offline, informational only, not affiliated with Supercell, no bypass/unblocked help).
All updated user-facing text is in English and is consistent across the Ask Fred page (intro, header helper text, and chat footer/helper line).

constraints: Do not add any external AI/LLM integrations or any network calls for Fred; responses must remain fully local and deterministic.
Do not implement, host, embed, proxy, or provide any mechanism to bypass network restrictions/paywalls/access controls (including "unblocked" gameplay guidance).
Do not modify any files under frontend/src/components/ui (read-only).
Keep changes within the existing single-actor backend architecture; no backend changes are required for this request.
nonGoals: Making Fred equivalent to ChatGPT in the general sense (open-domain knowledge, internet browsing, or non-deterministic generation).
Adding real-time chat, WebSockets, or external data sources for Fred.
Storing chat history on the backend or adding user accounts specifically for chat memory.
